sections.h2: Which Moore County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
The Moore County Tax Department handles it all, from listing and appraisal to billing and collection. The office is at 1 Courthouse Square in Carthage, NC 28327, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 5 pm, and the phone number is 910-947-2255. The mailing address is P.O. Box 457, Carthage.

The county's Tax page splits the work into divisions that follow the state statutes. Listing keeps ownership records and personal property accounts, and Appraising values land and buildings. Collecting has a current section for bills in their normal window and a delinquent section for past-due accounts.

  • Pay by mailing the coupon from your bill, in person at the Historic Courthouse, or online.
  • Pay by phone at 1-855-451-2620 with your bill number ready.
  • In-person payers can use cash, check, debit card or credit card.
  • Card and electronic check payments carry a convenience fee charged by the processor, InvoiceCloud.

Ask the Tax Department whether any town or district bill applies to your address in addition to the county bill.

sections.h2: How big is Moore County, and what do homes cost here?
sections.html:
Moore County had 110,619 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. It covers 697.68 square miles of land. Population grew 10.9% between the April 2020 base and mid-2025.

The 2020-2024 housing numbers explain why assessment values matter to owners here.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $351,400.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 76.4%.
  • Housing units, July 1, 2025: 52,979.
  • Median household income: $86,080.
  • Mean commute to work: 26.6 minutes.

When a typical home carries a six-figure assessment, even a small percentage error on the tax value adds up over the years. That makes it worth checking your property record card against what you know about the house.

sections.h2: When are Moore County property taxes due, and when do they become late?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due September 1 each year. State law sets the schedule in G.S. 105-360: tax paid before January 6 carries no interest, and tax paid on or after that date picks up 2% through the end of January, then three-fourths of one percent for each month after.

The January listing window matters for personal property. Personal property, including business equipment, is listed each year, and real estate is listed permanently once it is on the books (G.S. 105-307). The state's listing period begins the first business day of January and ends January 31, with limited extensions.

If your house sells in the fall, the bill that arrives for that year still has to be settled. Ask your closing attorney whether the tax will be prorated or paid in full from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: How often does Moore County revalue property?
sections.html:
Moore County revalues on a four-year cycle. The most recent revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, and the county FAQ says the next is scheduled for 2027, then every four years after, unless market conditions or state law call for a different schedule.

That is faster than the statewide minimum. North Carolina requires counties to reappraise all real property at least every eight years, and counties may set a shorter cycle by resolution (G.S. 105-286).

The county values property by mass appraisal, using cost, market and income approaches, with values set to the January 1 date of the revaluation year. Between revaluations the tax value does not move with the market. An appraiser may still visit after a building permit, a change to the parcel map, or a recorded sale whose price falls outside a set tolerance of the assessment. The county receives permit information from the county itself and from Aberdeen, Pinebluff, Pinehurst and Southern Pines.

Anything that adds heated square footage counts as an improvement, and so do decks, porches, patios, storage buildings, pools and barns. The owner is responsible for telling the Tax Department about improvements.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Moore County property value?
sections.html:
You file a signed written request or the county's appeal form with the Tax Department, and for real estate the window opens each January 1 and closes when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. The county advertises the adjournment in the local newspaper.

Moore County appeal paths by property type
Property typeWhen to appealHow
Real propertyFrom January 1 until the board adjournsSigned request or appeal form, informal review first, then the board
Personal property, business or notWithin 30 days of the bill dateSigned written request or personal property form
Registered motor vehicleWithin 30 days of the bill dateWritten request with signature; pay the bill on time anyway

The owner carries the burden of showing that the value is inequitable compared with surrounding properties or above fair market value, using cost, sales or income evidence from the lead-up to the revaluation date.

Beyond the county, state law lets you take a board decision to the Property Tax Commission by written notice filed within 30 days after the board mailed its decision (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What tax relief can Moore County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three programs for permanent residences, and an owner can receive benefit from only one of them. Moore County owners apply to the county tax office, not the State.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value is excluded for an owner who is 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, and meets the income limit (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4% of income at or under the limit and 5% for income above it up to 150% of the limit, with the excess deferred as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

The Department of Revenue prints the 2026 income limit as $38,800, with $58,200 as the 150% figure. Applications go on Form AV-9, should be filed in the listing period, and must be accepted through June 1 before the tax year.

If you sell or move out, circuit breaker deferred taxes for the previous three fiscal years come due, so the payoff belongs on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Moore County house with tax still owed?
sections.html:
The tax follows the parcel, so it has to be paid or paid off at closing. A lien for real property tax attaches as of the listing date (G.S. 105-355), and the county can enforce it by foreclosure, which is described in G.S. 105-374.

North Carolina tax foreclosure proceeds like a mortgage foreclosure action filed in the county. The sale is a public auction at the courthouse door, and an owner can redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

Selling before it reaches that stage is usually cheaper. Request a payoff from the Moore County Tax Department, check for any open municipal bill, and give the number to the closing attorney.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Moore County property tax?
faqs.a: You can pay at the Tax Department at 1 Courthouse Square in Carthage, by mail, online, or by phone at 1-855-451-2620. In person you can use cash, check, debit or credit card, and card payments carry a convenience fee.

faqs.q: When was Moore County last revalued?
faqs.a: The most recent revaluation took effect January 1, 2023. The county schedules the next one for 2027 and then every four years, unless the market or state law calls for a different schedule.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a personal property or vehicle value in Moore County?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date of the tax bill. File a signed written request with the Tax Department. For a vehicle, pay the bill when it is due anyway to avoid late penalties.

faqs.q: Does Moore County adjust property values when the market changes?
faqs.a: No. Tax value is set as of January 1 of the revaluation year and is not adjusted up or down between revaluations. New improvements, though, can lead to an appraiser visit and a changed value.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for the elderly or disabled homestead exclusion?
faqs.a: File Form AV-9 with the county tax office, not the Department of Revenue. The state asks for it during the January listing period but accepts it through June 1 before the tax year. You can receive only one of the three relief programs.
